intended_object: A helper that applies the forward direction of the hom-set bijection Hom(f⁻¹M, N) ≃ Hom(M, f_*N). Here f is a continuous map X → Y, M is a sheaf of S-modules on Y and N is a sheaf of f⁻¹S-modules on X. The docstring ("The actual forward bundled map") and its use in `homEquivCore`, `backward_forward` and `forward_backward` show what it is.
explanation:
The body is just `homEquiv f S M N g`, the forward direction of an equivalence the library has already built. It is named only so the proof that this equivalence is natural can be written as a `forward`/`backward` pair. That proof then feeds `Adjunction.CoreHomEquiv` and `Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv`, which together build the adjunction between the inverse-image module functor and the pushforward functor.

The forward direction of this bijection is the adjoint transpose, which does have mathematical meaning. But this declaration adds no mathematical content of its own: it is a named alias for `⇑(homEquiv f S M N)`, an internal device for the library's construction. Any mathematical content, and so any judgment of correctness or generality, belongs to `homEquiv`, `moduleFunctor` and `pushforwardFunctor`, not to this wrapper. For that reason it is classed as a technical device rather than a mathematical object.
